bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, building systems that learn from data and improve over time without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern technology, used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Tremendous growth due to large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised Learning, Unsupervised Learning, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trained on labeled data to predict outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Trained on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with its environment to maximize cumulative rewards (e.g., robotics, gaming).
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and minimize the difference between predictions and actual values.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for training the model and evaluating its performance on unseen data.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor performance on new data.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicts probability of class membership.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data into subsets based on feature values.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Assess performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, precision, MSE.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data by splitting into multiple subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Adjusting model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Many complex models (especially deep learning) are difficult to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair or unethical outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting model generalization and performance.
Continuously evolving with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will lead to more powerful, transparent, and interpretable systems.
Applications will become more integrated into daily life across various industries.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential as the field progresses.
